title: Two Commits on the Wrong Branch
symptom: You spent the morning on the search feature and were about to open a pull request from feature/search, but GitHub says that branch has nothing new on it. Nothing has been pushed yet. Put the work where it belongs and leave main as everyone else has it.

goals.description: The search commits are on feature/search, and main matches origin/main again

question.prompt: What happened, and why was the fix safe?
options: The commits were lost; they had to be rewritten
They were committed on main because feature/search was never checked out; moving the branch pointer and resetting main is safe because neither was pushed
Git put them on the wrong branch by mistake
They were pushed to main and must be reverted

debrief: 'Your branch is ahead of origin/main by 2 commits' said it all: the work was on main, because the branch was created but never switched to. A branch is only a pointer to a commit, so the fix is moving pointers, not copying work: point feature/search at the commits (git branch -f, or switch to it and git reset --hard main), then put main back where origin/main is. Both are safe here only because nothing was pushed; once commits are shared, you revert instead of moving pointers backwards. If feature/search had commits of its own, git cherry-pick would have copied the two commits across instead. Checking 'git status' before the first commit of a task is the habit that prevents this.
